blocks.content: PART A: CONCEPT OF INFLATION

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Inflation is a continuous and general increase in price levels that results in a decline in the purchasing power of money.
Inflation types based on speed include Creeping (<3%), Walking (3-10%), Galloping (very high), and Hyperinflation (uncontrollable).
Demand-pull inflation is caused by excess aggregate demand, while cost-push inflation is caused by rising production costs.
Inflation affects society unequally: fixed income groups and lenders lose, whereas borrowers may gain.
Inflation is controlled using RBI's monetary policy (raising CRR, SLR, Repo Rate) and government fiscal measures (increasing taxes, reducing spending).

blocks.content: 1. Meaning of Inflation

Inflation refers to a sustained, continuous and general increase in the price level of goods and services in an economy over a period of time. It does not mean a rise in the price of one good, but a rise in prices of most goods and services.
During inflation, the purchasing power of money falls. This means that with the same amount of money, people are able to buy fewer goods than before.
2. Key Characteristics of Inflation

• Inflation is a continuous process, not a one-time increase
• It involves a general rise in prices, not individual prices
• It leads to decline in purchasing power of money
• It affects the entire economy
PART B: TYPES OF INFLATION (VERY IMPORTANT)
3. Demand-Pull Inflation
Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand in the economy exceeds aggregate supply. When people have more money to spend but goods are limited, prices rise.
Causes include increase in money supply, rise in income, increased government expenditure and growth in population.
4. Cost-Push Inflation
Cost-push inflation occurs due to an increase in the cost of production. When wages, raw material prices, fuel costs or taxes increase, producers raise prices.
5. Creeping Inflation
Creeping inflation refers to a slow and mild rise in prices, usually less than 3% per year. It is considered normal and even helpful for economic growth.
6. Walking Inflation
During inflation, the purchasing power of money falls.
Walking inflation refers to a moderate rate of inflation, usually between 3% to 10%. If not controlled, it may turn into galloping inflation.
7. Galloping Inflation
Galloping inflation is a very high and rapid increase in prices. It creates economic instability and harms growth.
8. Hyperinflation
Hyperinflation is an extremely high and uncontrollable rate of inflation. Money loses its value almost completely. Example: Germany after World War I.
PART C: CAUSES OF INFLATION
9. Demand-Side Causes

• Excess money supply
• Increase in government expenditure
• Rise in population
• Increase in exports
• Hoarding and black money
10. Supply-Side Causes

Moderate rate; may turn into galloping inflation if uncontrolled

• Rise in cost of production

PART D: EFFECTS OF INFLATION
11. Effects on Different Sections of Society

• Fixed income groups suffer the most
• Borrowers gain while lenders lose
• Savers lose purchasing power
• Businessmen may gain initially
12. Effects on Economy

• Disturbs economic stability
• Worsens income inequality
• Discourages savings
• Encourages speculation
PART E: CONTROL OF INFLATION
13. Monetary Measures (RBI)

• Increase in CRR reduces money supply
• Increase in SLR restricts bank lending
• Increase in Repo Rate makes borrowing costly
• Open Market Operations absorb excess liquidity
14. Fiscal Measures (Government)

• Reduction in public expenditure
• Increase in taxes
• Control on deficit financing

items: Borrowers gain while lenders lose during inflation.
RBI curbs inflation by increasing Repo Rate, CRR, and SLR to reduce money supply and liquidity.
Creeping inflation (under 3% annually) is considered helpful for economic growth.

blocks.content: 15. Other Measures

• Increase in production
• Effective public distribution system
• Price controls and subsidies
PART F: INFLATION AND ECONOMIC GROWTH
16. Inflation vs Growth
Mild inflation may promote growth, but high inflation harms economic stability and growth.
SSC ULTRA FINAL REVISION POINTS

• Inflation = continuous rise in general prices
• Purchasing power of money falls
• Demand-pull = excess demand
• Cost-push = rising cost
• Hyperinflation destroys money value
• RBI controls inflation through monetary policy
